articles.title: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael, gave more than $25,000 worth of helmets, shoulder pads and footballs to Chelsea High School in Massachusetts
articles.summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his wife Ann Michael contribute over $25,000 worth of sports equipment to Chelsea High School, launching the Power Up Play Program to enhance youth sports opportunities in New England.
articles.body: Imagine wanting to play football but not having the gear to do it. That's the reality for many students around the world. Cost can be one of the many hurdles in their way. New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael, donated more than $25,000 worth of helmets, shoulder pads, and footballs to Chelsea High School in Massachusetts on October 28, 2026. According to The Patriot Ledger, the donation was made through the MayeDay Family Foundation and Good Sports, a Boston-based nonprofit. The gift also launched something more. It marks the start of a new programme that aims to help high school athletes across New England.A gift with a bigger goal The initiative is called the Power Up Play. It's a collaboration between the foundation and Good Sports to support after-school sports programmes at high schools in New England. The aim of this programme, according to the press release, extends beyond just providing sports equipment. It also hopes to help young athletes build confidence, resilience, and life skills that carry over in school and everyday life. The MayeDay Family Foundation is relatively new. It was founded by Drake and Ann in March 2026 for children and families in need. The foundation intends to fund programmes in New England, including Boston Children's Hospital, as well as in the couple's home state of North Carolina. It has been swift in its actions. In May, it organised its first event, a celebrity softball game in Polar Park, Worcester, Massachusetts, that raised over $500,000. In September, the Mayes donated $15,000 to fulfil the Amazon wish list of all teachers and support specialists at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Providence, Rhode Island.Why gear can be a barrier Joining a team is often more expensive than people expect. The C.S. Mott Children’s Hospital National Poll on Children’s Health, based at the University of Michigan, surveyed 961 parents who answered questions about 1,323 children in middle or high school. Its report from 2019 found the average cost of school sports, including fees, equipment, and travel, was $408. It was much more than arts, which was $251 and clubs or other activities, which was $126. The poll also found a gap by income. Students from households earning less than $100,000 a year did not participate in any school activities at twice the rate of students from higher-income families. Overall, 18% of students were not participating in any extracurricular activity. Many parents were not accessing help either. Only 7% had ever applied for a fee waiver or scholarship, and 19% said they didn't know how to. The poll is from 2019, so the costs might be different today.Why the teacher gift matters The Mayes’ help didn't stop at sports. Their September gift was for the teachers, and national data shows why that's important. A report from the National Center for Education Statistics, a part of the US Department of Education, examined how much public school teachers spend on classroom supplies without being reimbursed. In the 2014-15 school year, teachers spending their own money spent an average of $478 and a median of $297. Teachers of elementary grades spent an average of $525. In schools where 75% or more of the students are eligible for free or reduced-price lunch, teachers spend an average of $550 compared to the $434 in schools with 0-34% eligibility. These numbers are from a survey back in 2015-16; today’s numbers might be different. Still, they show why fulfilling teachers’ wish lists can matter.One gift will probably not break down all the barriers. Transportation and having a job were also cited in the Michigan poll as reasons students sit out, particularly among boys. It's too early to see how far Power Up Play will go, but the concept is easy to relate to. For some students, a helmet and a set of pads can be a little door to a much bigger world.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Camille Kostek reacts to Rob Gronkowski’s political controversy after former Patriots star faces New Hampshire speculation
articles.summary: Rob Gronkowski has rejected claims that he and Camille Kostek were supporting Turning Point USA during their Election Day visit to New Hampshire.
articles.body: Rob Gronkowski has rejected claims that he and Camille Kostek were supporting Turning Point USA during their Election Day visit to New Hampshire. The former New England Patriots tight end said the speculation was “upsetting and eye opening” after photos of the couple near a tent bearing the conservative group's logo began circulating online. Kostek, meanwhile, reposted Gronkowski's statement on Instagram, signaling her support for his response. The couple said they were simply greeting fans and taking pictures, not campaigning for a political organization.Camille Kostek backs Rob Gronkowski after political speculationGronkowski's statement came two days after the couple's appearance at polling locations in New Hampshire on November 3. The former NFL star and Kostek greeted fans, signed jerseys and posed for photos. Some of those interactions took place near a tent displaying the Turning Point USA logo, which led to questions about their political leanings.However, a spokesperson for Turning Point USA told CBS News that Gronkowski was not part of the organization's group. The spokesperson said the former tight end had walked past the tent.That distinction became central to Gronkowski's response. He wanted to make it clear that being photographed near the group did not mean he supported its political work.“It has been upsetting and eye opening to see the narratives around my visit to NH on Election Day with Camille,” Gronkowski said on Instagram on November 5.He then addressed the speculation directly.“In regard to the images and videos circulating we are not endorsed by or affiliated with Turning Point USA.”Kostek reposted his statement to her Instagram Story later that day. Her response was brief, but it showed that she stood behind Gronkowski as the couple tried to clear up the confusion.The incident also highlights how a few images can quickly shape public perception. A photo taken during an ordinary interaction may tell only part of the story, especially when it involves a public figure and a politically active organization.Gronkowski explains what happened in New HampshireGronkowski offered more detail about the visit, saying the couple had stopped at Goffstown High School before crossing the street to meet fans.“After stopping at Goffstown high school we crossed the street to greet excited fans yelling out our names before leaving to the next location. We simply took some pictures and I signed some things for them before leaving.”He also stressed that the couple had interacted with people from different political backgrounds that morning.The former Patriots star said they “took photos with people across the political spectrum throughout that morning” and added, “We cannot control what the media has made of it and running with — so we are here to shut down the false narratives.”Gronkowski was particularly unhappy with how the images had been presented. He called it “disappointing to see an innocent moment stripped of context and turned into clickbait.”He ended his message with a broader appeal, saying, “Our message has always been and always will be to treat everyone with kindness and hope you all will do the same.”New Hampshire voters were deciding two major races on Election Day, including a vacant U.S. Senate seat and the governor's race. Republican Gov. Kelly Ayotte narrowly defeated Democrat Cinde Warmington, while Chris Pappas defeated John Sununu to become the first openly gay man elected to the U.S. Senate.Against that political backdrop, Gronkowski and Kostek's appearance drew attention they say they never intended to attract. Their statement makes one thing clear: the couple wants their interactions with fans to remain separate from political endorsements.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2020, Patrick Mahomes bought a $3.37 million Texas mansion; 4 years later, its estimated value reached $5.5 million
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes paid $3.37 million for a Westlake, Texas mansion in March 2020. That was about $890,000 below the $4.26 million asking price.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes paid $3.37 million for a Westlake, Texas mansion in March 2020. That was about $890,000 below the $4.26 million asking price. Estimates now put the home near $5.5 million, a paper gain of roughly $2.1 million, or 63 percent, in four years. The house sits in the Dallas-Fort Worth corridor and was long the priciest property the Chiefs quarterback owned. Here is how the deal came together and what the number really means.How Patrick Mahomes turned a $3.37 million Texas mansion into a $5.5 million assetThe story starts with a discount. Reports say the home was listed at $4.26 million and came from the estate of Andrew Gissinger III, a former San Diego Chargers player. Mahomes closed for $3.37 million. On day one, he had already saved about 21 percent off the sticker price.The rest comes from a simple calculation. If the $5.5 million estimate holds, the house gained about $2.13 million over the purchase price. Spread across four years, that works out to roughly 13 percent a year. For a high-end property, that is a strong run.There is one catch, and it matters. The $5.5 million figure is an estimate, repeated across several media reports. It is not an appraisal and not a sale price. Nobody has paid that amount for the house. Until someone does, it stays a number on paper.What you get for the money in WestlakeThe property covers about 7,800 square feet, with four bedrooms and seven bathrooms. Reports put the cost at roughly $432 per square foot at purchase. At the $5.5 million estimate, that rises to around $705.The design leans modern farmhouse. Listing descriptions mention high ceilings, a floating staircase, a wet bar, a wine room and a game room. A private study leads up to a loft. Outside, the house has an infinity pool, a spa, an outdoor kitchen, a sunken grill area and a fire pit. It looks out over the Vaquero Golf Club.One detail is murky. A few outlets say the house was built in 2014, while others suggest it was new when Mahomes bought it. Others confuse it with his Missouri project. Treat the build year with caution. Everything else above appears consistently across reports.Why Westlake, and why that springTiming helps explain the choice. Mahomes won Super Bowl LIV in February 2020, and he bought the house a month later. That August he signed a 10-year, $450 million extension with the Chiefs. So the purchase came before the biggest contract in NFL history, not after it.Home also pulled at him. He grew up in Tyler, Texas, and played at Texas Tech, so a Texas base made sense for the offseason. Reports say he wanted more room for his growing family. His daughter Sterling arrived in 2021, and his son Bronze followed in 2022.The market worked in his favor too. Home prices across Texas climbed sharply in the years after 2020, and luxury homes near Dallas and Fort Worth were no exception. Mahomes did not predict that. But he bought a well-priced house in a place people kept wanting to live, and the timing did the rest.Is the $2 million gain actually profit?Not quite, and this is where a headline can mislead. A paper gain is not cash in hand. Selling a house this size brings agent fees, closing costs and taxes. Four years of upkeep on a pool, a large lawn and a big interior also eat into the return. Once those costs are counted, the real profit would be noticeably smaller than $2.13 million.Scale matters too. Against a $450 million contract, a $2 million gain is small. The more interesting point is how Mahomes handled his money. His Missouri portfolio, which reports link to an eight-acre plot in Belton bought for about $400,000, shows the same pattern. He tends to buy land or a discounted property, then build or wait.Reports on his holdings have also varied. Some outlets mix up purchase years, building years and values across his properties. If you are quoting numbers, check them against listing records or a named source. As of the reports reviewed here, no sale of the Westlake house has been reported, so the $5.5 million figure remains unproven.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes under fire as Travis Kelce sides against Patrick Mahomes' controversial Chiefs penalty controversy
articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes was not willing to stay silent after a costly officiating decision hurt the Kansas City Chiefs, but her criticism has not convinced
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes was not willing to stay silent after a costly officiating decision hurt the Kansas City Chiefs, but her criticism has not convinced everyone. Former Cincinnati Bengals star Chad Johnson has offered a very different take on the controversial call that wiped out Patrick Mahomes' potential game-winning touchdown against the Denver Broncos. While the Chiefs and their supporters questioned the timing of the flag, Johnson believes the officials had a legitimate reason to throw it. His comments have added another twist to an already heated debate surrounding Kansas City's narrow defeat.Chad Johnson disagrees with Brittany Mahomes over controversial Chiefs penaltyThe controversy erupted during the Chiefs' 28-24 loss to the Broncos on November 1. Kansas City had one final opportunity to steal the victory, with Patrick Mahomes leading the offence deep into Denver territory. Facing fourth-and-goal from the one-yard line, the quarterback connected with Rashee Rice for what appeared to be a dramatic winning touchdown.However, the celebrations did not last. Officials called right tackle Jaylon Moore for a false start, cancelling the score and ending Kansas City's comeback hopes.Brittany Mahomes quickly expressed her frustration on Instagram, questioning the decision that denied her husband a chance to secure the victory. Her reaction attracted attention, particularly because the penalty came during such a crucial moment.But Johnson was not persuaded by the argument that the officials had made a questionable call.Speaking on the 'Nightcap' podcast alongside Shannon Sharpe, the former NFL wide receiver watched the replay and gave his assessment.“Brittany Mahomes was not happy, and she posted it…. No bias here. Do you believe? Did he false start?” Sharpe asked.Johnson responded, “I saw the replay. He flinched. That’s a false start.”He also suggested that officials could have shown some restraint given the circumstances, although he did not dispute Moore's movement.“Now listen, as a referee, what you can do in that situation is you don’t want the game to end like that. You don’t have to call it because it was a minor flinch, but he did flinch. It’s clear as day.”Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce react to Chiefs' costly flagJohnson was not alone in his assessment. Sharpe also defended the ruling, explaining that offensive linemen cannot move once they have settled into their stance.Patrick Mahomes, meanwhile, admitted that he had not reviewed the footage when reporters asked him about the decision.“I have not seen it, but it didn’t surprise me or catch me or anything like that, so it couldn’t have been big, but it was called… I mean, at the end of the day, you have to go with whatever is called, but a lot of times in those big moments, the little stuff doesn’t get called like that.”Andy Reid also acknowledged noticing movement, saying, “I didn’t see it… I saw him move his head.”Interestingly, Travis Kelce shared Johnson's view during an episode of 'New Heights' with his brother Jason.“Yeah, he flinches.”The penalty was particularly costly for Kansas City, which finished the game with 11 flags for 105 yards. The defeat dropped the Chiefs to 5-2, leaving them behind Denver in the AFC West standings. What looked like a potential last-second victory instead became another talking point about officiating, discipline and the fine margins that can decide an NFL game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Guys like that are....": Tyreek Hill's return to Kansas City hits rock bottom as Chiefs have little reason to bring back former superstar
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs fans hoping for a Tyreek Hill reunion may have to prepare for disappointment.
articles.body: Kansas City Chiefs fans hoping for a Tyreek Hill reunion may have to prepare for disappointment. The possibility of seeing the explosive wide receiver back in red and gold is becoming increasingly difficult to imagine. Two major problems stand in his way: a lengthy recovery from a serious knee injury and a damaging civil court verdict. With November already here, Hill's chances of returning to the NFL this season appear to be fading fast. The Chiefs, meanwhile, have their own reasons to look elsewhere rather than pursue their former superstar.Tyreek Hill’s injury and legal troubles create major Chiefs comeback doubtsHill's situation has become increasingly complicated since his injury brought his 2025 campaign to an early end. The 31-year-old is still recovering from multiple torn knee ligaments and has yet to secure a contract with an NFL team.His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, had previously identified October as a possible return target. However, that timeline has passed without a comeback. According to RotoBaller, Hill remains unavailable, making him an unreliable option for fantasy football managers looking for help during the second half of the season.The legal situation has created another serious obstacle. A recent civil jury verdict found Hill liable on two counts related to domestic violence. The finding could make teams even more cautious about bringing him into their locker rooms.As reported by Heavy.com, the civil case has added another layer of uncertainty to his future. Even if Hill makes progress in his rehabilitation, a potential signing would involve more than simply assessing his physical condition.For a team considering a midseason addition, the combination of an uncertain recovery and legal complications presents a difficult decision.Patrick Mahomes and Chiefs have other options without Tyreek HillKansas City also has little reason to rush into a reunion. The Chiefs already have young receivers who were expected to become major contributors to Patrick Mahomes' offence.ESPN's Dan Graziano recently highlighted the team's existing talent while questioning the need to bring in another receiver."I know we do this all the time with the Chiefs, but they have guys. They just aren't playing to their potential. Rashee Rice was a second-round pick. Xavier Worthy was a first-round pick! Remember how mad everybody got at the Bills for letting the Chiefs move up to take him? Guys like that are supposed to be the solutions."His assessment points to a bigger issue within Kansas City's offence. Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy have the talent and draft pedigree to make a difference. The coaching staff needs to get more out of the players already on the roster.With the trade deadline adding pressure to teams looking for reinforcements, Hill's name may attract attention from fans. However, Kansas City appears better positioned to develop its current receivers than gamble on an injured veteran facing legal challenges.For now, a return to Arrowhead looks increasingly unlikely. Hill's NFL future remains uncertain, and the Chiefs have reasons to focus on the answers already in their building.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: The $8.66 million move Ravens made to finalize Jacoby Brissett trade
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens restructured defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike’s contract to clear $8.66 million in salary-cap space and facilitate their trade for Jaco...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens restructured defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike's contract to clear $8.66 million in salary-cap space and facilitate their trade for Jacoby Brissett . They also released quarterback Austin Reed after finalizing the deal.

Baltimore acquired Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Arizona Cardinals on Friday for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero shared an update on X, formerly Twitter, explaining the financial adjustment that helped the Ravens complete the deal.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Another Ravens note: The team converted most of DT Nnamdi Madubuike 's remaining base salary to a signing bonus, clearing $8.66 million in 2026 cap space to give them breathing room and facilitate the Brissett trade."

ESPN's Adam Schefter additionally took to the platform Saturday to report the corresponding roster move.

Reed backed up Joe Fagnano in Thursday's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars but has yet to play a regular-season NFL snap. Fagnano made his NFL debut last Sunday.

Reed's release ends his latest stint with the Ravens, who brought him back this week. The former Western Kentucky quarterback joined Baltimore in August before the team waived him during final roster cuts.

He went undrafted in 2024 and spent time on the Chicago Bears' practice squad. Before arriving in Baltimore, he started all 10 UFL games for the Renegades.

Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are on injured reserve after getting hurt in the Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Jackson injured his right thumb and could miss the remainder of the season, while Huntley's turf toe is reportedly season-ending.

The Ravens have lost four straight games to fall to 4-5. Brissett, 33, brings 73 career starts across 11 NFL seasons and likely will make his Baltimore debut in Week 10 vs. the Los Angeles Chargers.

articles.title: San Francisco 49ers’ $27M injury loss: Mike Evans, Nick Bosa and Christian McCaffrey’s Week 9 status ahead of Las Vegas Raiders clash
articles.summary: RotoWire’s November 3 report identifies the San Francisco 49ers as the most injured team of the 2026 NFL season. Kyle Shanahan’s team ranks No.
articles.body: RotoWire’s November 3 report identifies the San Francisco 49ers as the most injured team of the 2026 NFL season. Kyle Shanahan’s team ranks No. 1 among all 32 franchises, with 23 players listed as out.San Francisco has been hit hardest by injuries to key players, including Nick Bosa and Christian McCaffrey. The 49ers’ cap hit out is nearly $50 million. Their figure stands at $49.7 million, the 10th-highest in the league, led by Nick Bosa’s $23 million cap number, according to RotoWire.According to Niners Wire’s Oliver G., the 49ers have lost nearly $27 million in player value due to injuries, the seventh-highest total in the NFL. The November 6 report puts their estimated player-value loss at $26.9 million.Despite being the NFL’s most injury-affected team, San Francisco boasts six wins and only one loss. The 49ers sit atop the NFC West - gladly trying to take over the Seattle Seahawks [4-4], Los Angeles Rams [4-4], and the Arizona Cardinals [3-5] little by little, week by week.San Francisco wideout Mike Evans injury updateMike Evans suffered rib and oblique injuries during the San Francisco 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals. He took a brutal hit to the ribs from Cardinals safety Budda Baker during the second quarter of the September 27 game.Despite suffering two broken ribs, the Texas A&M alum returned to action in the following weeks, only to be sidelined by another injury.Evans had been dealing with Achilles tendinitis in the week leading up to the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Washington Commanders. He tried to play through it but experienced a flare up late in the first half, forcing him to leave the game.The San Francisco wideout did not return to action. Evans subsequently missed the Week 7 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.Although Week 8 was a bye week, he did not recover sufficiently to return to practice. The veteran receiver did not participate in any of the three practice sessions ahead of the Week 9 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders. He was officially ruled out on November 6.Christian McCaffrey injuryChristian McCaffrey suffered a mild hamstring strain during the first drive of the San Francisco 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. He briefly exited the game but later returned to play a limited role. The Week 8’s bye came at the right moment for the running back.McCaffrey sat out Wednesday’s practice ahead of the Week 9 clash vs. the Las Vegas Raiders. However, he returned as a limited participant on Thursday. He upgraded to full participation on Friday. He received no injury designation, meaning he is cleared to play in the Week 9 matchup against the Raiders at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California.Nick Bosa injuryNick Bosa suffered a left calf strain during pre-practice warmups ahead of Week 3 of the 2026 season. He missed the following five games from Weeks 3 through 7. The star defensive end admitted that the injury took longer than expected to heal because he had been overcompensating with his left leg due to preexisting tendinitis in his right knee.The Week 8 bye provided additional recovery time for Bosa. He was a limited participant in Wednesday and Thursday’s practices. He upgraded to full participation on Friday ahead of the Week 9 clash against the Las Vegas Raiders. articles.title: Lamar Jackson's Ravens Future Discussed by NFL Insider Amid Rumors on Contract Status
articles.summary: Despite the fact that the Baltimore Ravens and quarterback Lamar Jackson have yet to agree to a new contract, there is reportedly mutual interest in the two sides remaining together long term.
articles.body:
Despite the fact that the Baltimore Ravens and quarterback Lamar Jackson have yet to agree to a new contract, there is reportedly mutual interest in the two sides remaining together long term.

According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, "there is no reason to believe" Jackson won't be back with the Ravens next year, as the Ravens have publicly declared that they "love him and want to keep him long term."

Jones noted that although it is "anyone's guess" when a contract extension may be reached, the two sides have to figure something out in the not-too-distant future.

Jackson is only signed through 2027, and he is currently set to have a salary cap hit of $84.3 million next season. On top of that, $42.47 million in void-year cap hits are set to activate from 2028 to 2030.

With all of that in mind, it would behoove the Ravens to sign Jackson to a new deal before the 2027 season since it would allow the organization to structure the deal in such a way that it would offer immediate cap relief.

The 29-year-old Jackson is a four-time Pro Bowler, three-time First Team All-Pro and two-time NFL MVP who has spent his entire nine-year NFL career in Baltimore.

While he is a dynamic force when healthy, Jackson missed four games last season and has been limited to five games so far this season due to injury.

After an ankle injury cost him three games, Jackson returned to start against the Buffalo Bills last week, but he injured his thumb on the Ravens' first offensive play of the game.

Jackson was subsequently placed on injured reserve, and head coach Jesse Minter told reporters the injury was "potentially" season-ending.

If that proves to be the case, the 4-5 Ravens may be hard-pressed to make the playoffs even after the acquisition of veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals this week.

That would mark Baltimore's second consecutive season outside the playoffs, largely due to Jackson's unavailability.

While Jackson's durability is likely something the Ravens have to take under consideration, there is almost no chance of them finding a better option any time soon, which seemingly makes Jackson and the Ravens agreeing to a new contract at some point the most realistic scenario.

articles.title: New Colts Rumors on Keenan Allen, Josh Downs, Grover Stewart Trade Talks at 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are reportedly fielding offers for multiple players ahead of Tuesday's upcoming NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are reportedly fielding offers for multiple players ahead of Tuesday's upcoming NFL trade deadline.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , wide receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, and defensive tackle Grover Stewart are among the Colts players generating interest.

The Colts have reportedly told interested teams that they have already received an offer of a fourth-round pick for Downs, although their initial asking price was a third-rounder.

Allen has reportedly also been "the subject of some inquiries," and is "another name to watch."

As for Stewart, he is also drawing interest, but the Colts are "aiming high with teams feeling like the price is more than they would give right now."

The 2-6 Colts have already traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers, but they seem to be taking a more measured approach with their other trade chips.

That includes star running back Jonathan Taylor, who has been the subject of rumors, although Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported Saturday that Taylor staying in Indianapolis is the "most likely outcome."

Downs, selected in the third round of the 2023 NFL draft out of North Carolina, set career highs with 72 receptions for 803 yards and five touchdowns in 2024, but his production has declined since then.

In eight games this season, he has caught 30 passes for 330 yards and one score.

Downs is a dynamic playmaker out of the slot when he is at his best, though, and contending teams in need of a slot receiver could potentially get a steal if he goes for a fourth-rounder.

Allen, 34, is a 14-year NFL veteran who is approaching the end of his career, although he remains a sure-handed and reliable option.

The six-time Pro Bowler has not topped 1,000 yards receiving in a season since 2023, but he had over 700 yards each of the past two seasons, and has made 36 catches for 325 yards and one touchdown so far this season.

Stewart, 33, is in the final year of his contract, and he has recorded 26 tackles, two tackles for loss and a half-sack in eight games this season.

More of a run-stopper than a pass-rusher with only 13.5 career sacks, the 6'4", 315-pound lineman could be a nice addition for a contending team that struggles to stop opposing rushing attacks.

articles.title: New Chiefs Rumors on 'Big-Name' WR Pursuit Amid Brian Thomas Jr., Josh Downs Trade Buzz
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are assessing their options at wide receiver ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, according to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are assessing their options at wide receiver ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, according to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones .

Jones reported that Kansas City is looking for a "big-name receiver" but have been "checking on everyone."

Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs has been the player most frequently linked to Kansas City. Downs has provided the Colts with consistent production since he was selected in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft, but Indianapolis is clearly looking to sell off any valuable assets to acquire draft capital. Downs has 30 receptions for 330 yards and one touchdown through eight games this season.

Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. has also been floated in trade rumors. The Jaguars have been hesitant to trade Thomas, but teams across the league don't believe the 24-year-old will be in Jacksonville for much longer, according to Jones.

"The Jaguars have held firm in keeping wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.," Jones wrote. "We'll see if they keep that posture after Thursday. The rest of the league seems certain the Jags will part with Thomas."

Thomas, a first-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, compiled 87 receptions for 1,282 receiving yards with 10 touchdowns in his rookie campaign. With the arrival of head coach Liam Coen the following season, the 24-year-old found himself slowly being phased out of Jacksonville's offensive game plan. He played only 19 snaps during Jacksonville's 33-10 victory against the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night Football, and he has just one reception for 12 yards and a score over the past four games.

The Chiefs wide receiving corps has continued to plague the team. Wide receivers Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy have been inconsistent, and the Chiefs lost deep-ball threat Tyquan Thornton to a gruesome injury in Week 4. None of Kansas City's receivers have eclipsed 250 receiving yards or caught more than two touchdowns this season.

The Chiefs offense has largely been effective due to its rushing attack, but a legitimate receiving threat could significantly help elevate the Chiefs offense.

articles.title: Colts reportedly entertaining Daniel Jones trade discussions ahead of deadline
articles.summary: Indianapolis has already shipped off LG Quenton Nelson and DT DeForest Buckner, and it's reportedly open to dealing RB Jonathan Taylor, too.
articles.body:
Multiple teams have inquired about the availability of quarterback Daniel Jones, and the Indianapolis Colts are engaging in those trade talks, ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Saturday .

The Minnesota Vikings are speculated to be among the other teams considering Jones, according to the ESPN and NFL Network report, as Jones spent part of the 2024 season in Minnesota and has familiarity with a Kevin O'Connell offense that's struggled with Kyler Murray under center.

Jones is set to start for Indianapolis at home against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. This past offseason, the Colts inked the 2019 No. 6 overall pick to a two-year, $88 million extension that reportedly included a $44 million signing bonus.

Since, however, Jones — who was coming off a season-ending Achilles tear — hasn't replicated the promising success he achieved during the Colts' 8-2 start to the 2025 campaign, and Indianapolis has moved on from longtime general manager Chris Ballard midseason , embarking on a franchise reset.

On Oct. 27, more than a week following Ballard's firing, the Colts traded Nelson and Buckner. They were two of the organization's longest-tenured players. The six-time All-Pro Nelson went to the Seattle Seahawks in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. And the two-time All-Pro Buckner landed back with his old team, the San Francisco 49ers , who gave up a 2027 fourth-round draft pick for the interior defensive lineman.

Indianapolis has dropped four games in a row and is 2-6, sitting in third place in an AFC South the Jacksonville Jaguars are running away with.

With Tuesday's trade deadline fast approaching, eyes are on the Colts, who could make their next move imminently under the direction of interim GM Ed Dodds and the supervision of owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon.

As for Jones, it's possible Indianapolis doesn't move him midseason. The Colts are expected to take calls on him through Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline, according to the ESPN and NFL Network report that surfaced Saturday.

The report also noted Jones has a $10.51 million injury guarantee for the 2027 season that, if he's still on Indianapolis' roster by March 15, will become fully guaranteed. Jones reportedly could waive that injury guarantee to help complete a potential trade.

Or, if the Colts don't trade him, the injury guarantee could be a reason they ultimately bench him, so they don't risk injury and, in turn, that $10.51 million guarantee.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders Posts Hype Video Ahead of 1st Browns Start of 2026 NFL Season vs. Saints
articles.summary: Ahead of his first start of the 2026 regular season, Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders posted a hype video on Saturday.
articles.body:
Ahead of his first start of the 2026 regular season, Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders posted a hype video on Saturday.

Along with the caption, "Thank you GOD $²," Sanders posted the video, which includes highlights from his NFL career thus far, on his Instagram account:

Sanders has served as Deshaun Watson's backup this season, but with Watson in concussion protocol , the former University of Colorado standout is getting the start on the road against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday.

Selected in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL draft, Sanders appeared in eight games and started seven of them as a rookie, going 3-4, and completing 56.6 percent of his passes for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions, while also rushing for 169 yards and a score.

After missing the entire 2025 season with an Achilles injury, Watson healed up and returned to compete with Sanders for the starting job during the preseason.

Watson won the competition, and although many considered it a controversial decision by head coach Todd Monken, it has paid dividends thus far.

The Browns have been one of the NFL's most pleasant surprises so far this season with a record of 5-3, and Watson has largely played well, completing 65.5 percent of his passing attempts for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three picks to go along with 217 yards and a touchdown on the ground.

Sanders has played sparingly this season as a result of Watson's solid performances, but it will be up to the second-year signal-caller on Sunday to keep things rolling for the playoff-contending Browns.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Jaguars' Pursuit of Defensive 'Playmaker' Ahead of 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars have made calls around the league to inquire about adding a playmaker to their defense, ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars have made calls around the league to inquire about adding a playmaker to their defense, ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported on Saturday.

The Jaguars lost nose tackle DaVon Hamilton and safety Eric Murray to season-ending injuries. Both players have played key roles on Jacksonville's defense, but losing Hamilton could be significant for a unit that has allowed the second-fewest points per game (15.1) and the fifth-fewest rushing yards per game (89.3) through the first half of the 2026 season.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that Jacksonville was already looking for interior defensive line help prior to the injury. "That need only amplifies with Hamilton out," Fowler wrote.

The Jaguars have been aggressive on the trade market over the past two seasons. They moved up to the No. 2 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft to select two-way star Travis Hunter, and they acquired wide receiver Jakobi Meyers before the trade deadline last year. The Meyers acquisition helped transform the offense, and Jacksonville won its final eight games of the regular season.

The Jaguars could also offer wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. in a potential trade for a defensive player. They have received "multiple inquiries" for the 24-year-old wide receiver, according to Schefter and Rapoport.

If Jacksonville wants to make any moves, it'll have to move quickly. The NFL's trade deadline is on Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Saints' Jordyn Tyson Reportedly Set to Make NFL Debut vs. Browns After Hamstring Injury
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson will make his NFL debut against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson will make his NFL debut against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz .

Tyson was selected with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but a hamstring injury landed him on injured reserve during training camp.

The Saints need to activate the rookie from injured reserve by Saturday afternoon for him to be eligible to play on Sunday. New Orleans has a 2-5 record, but remains in contention in a relatively weak NFC South.

The Saints are in last place in their division but sit only one game behind the Carolina Panthers, who currently lead the NFC South with a 3-4 record. With a defensive unit that has struggled throughout the season, New Orleans will need to lean on its offense to pull out a few wins.

Saints wide receivers Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele has served as the team's top wideouts, but New Orleans hasn't been able to find consistent production from a third wide receiver.

Olave has reeled in 49 receptions for 636 receiving yards with two touchdowns, while Vele has 33 catches for 348 receiving yards with three touchdowns. No other Saints wide receiver has reached 10 receptions or 100 receiving yards through seven games.

Tyson has a significant injury history dating back to his time at Colorado and Arizona State. He only played every regular-season game in one of his four collegiate seasons. If the rookie can stay healthy moving forward, he could help the Saints establish a more versatile passing attack and draw defensive coverage away from Olave.

New Orleans has struggled to run the ball, but could also see its rushing attack bolstered with left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. and running back Travis Etienne Jr. returning from stints on the injured reserve list. Banks is listed as questionable for Sunday, but Etienne has not yet returned to practice.

articles.title: Browns' Deshaun Watson Clears Concussion Protocol, Updated Game Status with Shedeur Set as QB1
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has cleared concussion protocol ahead of Shedeur Sanders' first start of the season Sunday at the New Orleans Saints, the team announced Saturday.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has cleared concussion protocol ahead of Shedeur Sanders' first start of the season Sunday at the New Orleans Saints, the team announced Saturday.

Watson remains questionable ahead of Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff, according to the Browns.

Browns head coach Todd Monken announced Friday Sanders would start against the Saints. Dillon Gabriel is on track to serve as Sanders' backup if Watson is ruled out ahead of the game.

The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson had been placed in concussion protocol after experiencing symptoms the day after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit in last Sunday's loss at the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Monken said Friday the decision to name Sanders starter was made in part because Watson, even if cleared by Sunday, had been unable to practice in the days leading up to the game.

NFL regulations dictate players in concussion protocol can't return to contact practices until they are cleared for participation by both a club physician and an independent consultant.

"He's still not able to do any team reps," Monken said Friday about Watson. "He can do individual, he can do some routes. Been in meetings, but you're notable to do any of the team reps, which makes it difficult."

The Browns have a recent history of players passing concussion protocol within a week of placement in the process. Cleveland reinstated KC Concepcion , Grant Delpit and Tytus Howard on similar timelines earlier this season.

Monken said Friday he hadn't yet decided if Watson would be backing up Sanders even if he cleared protocol by this weekend.

He also said he felt Sanders had benefitted from the experience he gained while competing with Watson for the QB1 job this summer.

"I liked his confidence. Liked the way he operated. Looked very comfortable in terms of getting our guys in and out of the huddle... and I thought he threw the ball extremely well," Monken said about Sanders in practice this week.

"I do think there is positives to the amount of reps he got during the fall... if a player is diligent, like he's been, you expect there to be some carryover."

ESPN and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Friday he didn't feel Watson's job was "in jeopardy" based on Sanders' performance.

Given that Watson is on expiring contract while Sanders is in the second year of his rookie deal, however, whether Sanders is able to help the Browns fight for the top of the AFC North could potentially impact the quarterback's future with the team.

articles.title: Ryan Clark accuses ESPN of targeting Troy Aikman as Joe Buck secures $108 million deal amid contract dispute
articles.summary: Ryan Clark has accused ESPN of creating a negative image of Troy Aikman as the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback faces an uncertain future with the
articles.body: Ryan Clark has accused ESPN of creating a negative image of Troy Aikman as the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback faces an uncertain future with the network. Speaking on The Pivot podcast, Clark said he believes ESPN is allowing negative stories about Aikman to shape public opinion instead of addressing his contract situation directly. Having recently lost his own job at ESPN, Clark says he recognises the pattern.Ryan Clark calls out ESPN over Troy Aikman’s contract situation and Joe Buck’s new dealClark shared his thoughts on the November 6 episode of The Pivot, where he questioned why ESPN had not shown the same public support for Aikman that it had shown other on-air personalities.He began by praising Aikman and his longtime broadcasting partner Joe Buck, who have worked together for 25 years.“But I look at Troy Aikman and Joe Buck. I believe they’re the best booth in football, and for 25 years, they’ve proved that,” Clark said. He also credited the pair for helping ESPN secure better NFL games and its first Super Bowl broadcast.Clark then raised concerns about the stories surrounding Aikman, including reports of tension between the two broadcasters.“Somebody is trying to make Troy Aikman look like the b*****d son,” he said.The former NFL safety believes the network’s handling of the situation is creating an image of Aikman as the problem, even though the full story has not been made public.“You mentioned the leaks. I’ve been around there. I know how it starts to happen when they’re trying to build a narrative about you,” Clark explained.He added that ESPN had previously supported people publicly, even when they made mistakes, but he had not seen the same response in Aikman’s case.“They haven’t done that for Troy,” Clark said. “So I do feel like there is a push to make him the bad guy, whether he is or not.”The contract situation has become more complicated since Buck agreed to a reported six-year, $108 million extension with ESPN in September. Aikman, meanwhile, is approaching the end of his five-year, $90 million agreement, signed in 2022. According to Front Office Sports, ESPN has not made him a formal offer, while his representatives reportedly proposed a return with a raise similar to Buck’s.ESPN has said it will not discuss talent contracts publicly before the Super Bowl.Ryan Clark connects Troy Aikman’s ESPN treatment to his own sudden firingClark’s criticism also comes from his own experience with ESPN. The network ended its relationship with him on July 20 after 11 years, informing him about the decision while he was appearing on NFL Live.According to The Athletic, ESPN had initially planned to tell Clark the following morning but changed its plans because executives were concerned that news of his departure might leak.Clark believes the way his exit was handled helps him understand what Aikman could be facing now.“I know that they have ways of maneuvering to protect people, and I know that they have ways of putting people in positions where a narrative is built around them, so when they make their exit, they can seem like the good guys. Because I was a part of that. This is what this feels like to me,” he said.Meanwhile, Aikman has already spoken about his uncertain future. During an appearance on Dallas radio station 96.7 The Ticket, he said he planned to finish the season before becoming a free agent.He also admitted that there was a 50-50 chance he would not return to television next season.Despite the uncertainty, Aikman and Buck are expected to work together through Super Bowl LXI on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium. Whether they continue as ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcasting team after that remains unclear.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Karrueche Tran is speaking out against people who keep asking when she plans to have children with her boyfriend, Deion Sanders. The 38-year-old actress says the repeated questions are hurtful, especially when people have no idea what she may be dealing with privately. Although she would love to become a mother, Tran says she is still working through some personal questions and wants people to respect that.Karrueche Tran calls baby questions rude as Deion Sanders’ girlfriend opens up about motherhoodDuring an appearance on The Pop Exchange Show, Tran explained how uncomfortable she feels when people repeatedly tell her to have a baby. She said that while she does want children, there are personal matters she is still trying to understand.“People comment, because they’re always commenting, you need to have a baby, da-da-da-da-da-da. And it’s like, you don’t know what’s going on in my life. I want to have a kid, but I am figuring my business out. And there’s a potential possibility that I can’t even have kids. So why are you even suggesting, or it’s just nasty?” she said.Tran made it clear that she is not against becoming a mother. In fact, she loves children and would be happy to have a family of her own. However, she does not appreciate strangers making assumptions about such a personal part of her life.“I think it’s just so rude and inconsiderate,” she added.The actress also spoke about the thoughts she has been dealing with as she approaches 40. At 38, she is thinking about whether motherhood will be part of her future, but she does not want outside pressure to make that decision even harder.“I would love to be a mother. I love kids. And that’s like a big thing that I’m going through right now, of like being 38 and coming to the realization if I’m going to have kids or not.”Her comments also bring attention to the fact that wanting children and knowing whether it will be possible are two different things. Tran has not shared a specific medical reason behind her concerns, and she has made it clear that people should not assume they know her situation.Deion Sanders opens up about having another child with Karrueche TranWhile Tran has spoken about her feelings on motherhood, Sanders has also shared his thoughts about becoming a father again. The Colorado Buffaloes head coach already has five children from his previous relationships and has experienced different stages of raising a family.During an appearance on The Pregame Network podcast, Sanders discussed the possibility of having another child. His response showed that he is not particularly interested in starting the parenting journey again at this stage of his life.“Like if I wanted another little, bad, ignorant, hateful, snotty-nosed, spunky Shilo. If I wanted another one of them, I could go reverse it and get that. But as the boss said, I’m Billy Blanks. I ain’t got time for this,” Sanders said.He also spoke about the financial responsibility that comes with raising children, making it clear that having another baby would mean taking on a major commitment.“And kids ain’t cheap. All y’all cost. Right now. I’m not talking about earlier on. I don’t need another little punky Shilo. You think I want another Shilo? I don’t want to be grand daddy going to pick up my baby,” he added.Sanders has five children, Deiondra Sanders, Deion Sanders Jr., Shilo Sanders, Shedeur Sanders and Shelomi Sanders. His eldest daughter, Deiondra, also became a mother in 2024, making him a grandfather.The relationship between Sanders and Tran first attracted attention in 2025 when the actress stood by him during his bladder cancer treatment. articles.title: Urban Meyer reveals how Steve Spurrier’s South Carolina win nearly broke him before Jarvis Moss saved Florida’s championship hopes
articles.summary: Urban Meyer has opened up about one of the hardest periods of his coaching career, revealing how Florida fans turned against him after a painful loss to
articles.body: Urban Meyer has opened up about one of the hardest periods of his coaching career, revealing how Florida fans turned against him after a painful loss to South Carolina in 2005. The former Gators coach recalled being booed at his own radio show and receiving hateful messages telling him to leave Gainesville. The experience became so difficult that he began worrying about his family’s future if results did not improve.Urban Meyer reveals how Florida fans turned against him after Steve Spurrier’s 2005 winSpeaking on A Peek Inside Florida Football on November 4, Meyer looked back at his early days in Gainesville and explained how much the criticism affected him. Florida had lost 30-22 to South Carolina on November 12, 2005, ending its 14-game winning streak against the Gamecocks. It was also a special win for Steve Spurrier, who was coaching South Carolina after spending 12 seasons leading Florida.For Meyer, the defeat was difficult for another reason. Spurrier was still a much-loved figure in Gainesville, having led the Gators to their first national championship in 1996. Meyer was trying to build his own legacy while dealing with the pressure of following one of the most successful coaches in the program’s history.The reaction from fans was something Meyer had not expected. Recalling the experience, he said, “I remember the year before when we lost to South Carolina. I went to my radio show, and I got booed.”He also spoke about how the criticism followed him beyond the stadium. “We lost a few games, and you know, Shelley didn’t feel it as much as I did. I couldn’t stand it. You know, I just didn’t feel welcome. I lost to Alabama, lost to LSU, and I couldn’t really go anywhere. Imagine walking into your radio show and getting booed.”The messages he received made the situation even harder. “Emails and letters and Nancy would try to hide them from me,” Meyer said. “You know, about get the hell out of the town and you don’t belong here, and so it was rugged.”He described that period as miserable, admitting that the hostility made it difficult to enjoy life outside football.Jarvis Moss’ block against Steve Spurrier’s South Carolina saved Urban Meyer’s Florida careerA year after the loss, Meyer got another chance to face Spurrier, this time at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium on November 11, 2006. Florida needed a win to secure its place in the SEC Championship Game, but South Carolina made the contest extremely close.The Gamecocks held a 16-10 lead in the fourth quarter before quarterback Chris Leak connected with Dallas Baker for a 21-yard touchdown. Florida took a 17-16 lead, but South Carolina still had an opportunity to win.With eight seconds left, Ryan Succop lined up for a 48-yard field goal. Defensive end Jarvis Moss broke through and blocked the kick, securing Florida’s one-point victory.That win helped Florida finish its SEC East campaign undefeated. The Gators later defeated Arkansas 38-28 in the SEC Championship Game and beat Ohio State 41-14 to win the national championship.However, Meyer revealed that his thoughts at the time were far from celebrating a possible title.“I wasn’t thinking national title,” he recalled. “I was thinking about the ramifications on my family, on me, on our program. And I looked at the livelihood of my family, myself. And the reality was that if we lose this one now, this is going to be tough to rally back.”The memory also comes as Florida tries to recover from a difficult start under first-year head coach Jon Sumrall. The Gators were 5-3 heading into their November 7 game against Oklahoma after losing 27-8 to Georgia on October 31.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

Now, former ESPN SportsCenter anchor Linda Cohn has questioned how both women chose to share their complaints. Cohn said that being married to an NFL quarterback does not stop them from having opinions, but it also does not protect them from criticism. She had a simple message for the two women: “Know the room.” Her comments come after both wives received negative reactions from football fans on social media.Brittany Mahomes questions officials after Kansas City Chiefs lose to Denver BroncosThe incident happened during Kansas City's 28-24 defeat to the Denver Broncos on November 1. With only seconds left, Patrick Mahomes connected with Rashee Rice for what appeared to be a winning touchdown. However, officials called a false start on Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore. The penalty wiped out the score and pushed Kansas City back five yards. Denver then stopped the Chiefs on the final play to secure the win.Brittany did not hide her frustration with the decision. She questioned why officials would make such a call on a potential game-winning touchdown and suggested the Chiefs were being treated differently.She wrote on Instagram: “You can't tell me you call that on a game-winning TD, oh wait yeah I can cause it's us.”She followed that message with another comment: “That was the weakest call I have ever seen.”Her reaction also drew attention because the Chiefs had suffered their second straight defeat. However, the discussion soon moved beyond the penalty itself, with fans questioning her suggestion that the team was being unfairly treated.Kelly Stafford's complaint about the Los Angeles Rams schedule also draws Linda Cohn's attentionKelly Stafford had raised a different concern just days earlier. Matthew Stafford's wife questioned the NFL's decision to give the Los Angeles Rams a shorter break before their Thanksgiving Eve game against the Green Bay Packers on November 25.The Rams are scheduled to face the Arizona Cardinals on November 15 before hosting Green Bay 10 days later. Kelly questioned the decision and wrote on her Instagram Story:“Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week.”She also explained why she felt the schedule was tiring, even for someone who watches from the stands.“Because after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season… and I have never played a single snap. I'm tired just watching from the stands. Can't imagine how the guys feel.”Her main concern was the time players get to recover between games. However, there is one detail worth noting: the Packers also have the same 10-day gap before their November 25 meeting with the Rams. So, Los Angeles is not the only team facing that shorter break.Linda Cohn understood Kelly's concern about player recovery but felt her personal comment about being tired from watching games could be difficult for ordinary fans to relate to.Cohn explained that NFL players face physical demands and need enough time to recover. However, she also asked Kelly to consider people who work long hours, look after their families and deal with everyday expenses before sitting down to watch football.Speaking about both women, Cohn said: “Marriage to a quarterback doesn't disqualify you from commentary, from having an opinion. It also doesn't exempt your commentary from criticism. Kelly and Brittany are two people making public statements.”She then shared the message that became the main point of her criticism:“Sometimes before you hit post, the most useful question is, how is this going to sound to somebody whose life looks very, very different from my own? Three words, know the room.”Cohn also made it clear that Kelly had raised an important issue about player recovery. She said: “Kelly makes the case for player recovery that's a conversation worth having. Just understand why your own game day exhaustion might not generate the sympathy you expect.”For Cohn, the issue was not whether Brittany and Kelly had the right to speak. It was how their words might sound to people who experience football and everyday life very differently.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Lions' Jack Campbell Placed on IR After Being Hospitalized with Neck Injury
articles.summary: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has been placed on injured reserve after suffering a serious neck injury that led to his hospitalization last Sunday.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has been placed on injured reserve after suffering a serious neck injury that led to his hospitalization last Sunday.

The Lions announced Campbell's designation Saturday ahead of a Sunday afternoon game at the Miami Dolphins.

Campbell said in a Wednesday statement he had "full movement" in his lower body and is "continuing to make progress with movement" in his upper body.

"I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic," Campbell said in his update. "I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better."

The Lions said, as of Monday, Campbell remained in a local hospital. Head coach Dan Campbell said in his latest update on Friday the linebacker "continues to improve."

"This is about, how would he prepare, how would he play?" the head coach said Friday. "Those are the standards for us going into this game. We owe it to him."

Campbell suffered his injury while attempting a tackle in the fourth quarter of the Lions' win over the Vikings. He did not move after falling and was treated by medical staff on the field before being carted off.

After racking up a career-high 176 tackles and receiving his first First-Team All-Pro selection last season, Campbell agreed to a four-year, $81 million extension that runs through the 2030 season.

Campbell led the Lions with 54 tackles, including one for loss, in six contests heading into last Sunday's game.

Veteran linebackers Derrick Barnes and Malcolm Rodriguez will be handling communication duties between the Lions defense and coordinator Kelvin Sheppard in Campbell's absence, per DetroitLions.com's Tim Twentyman .

The Lions will hope that system allows the team to build on its 5-2 start to the season and continue competing for the top spot in the NFC North when Sunday's matchup kicks off at 1 p.m. ET in Miami.

articles.title: Saints activate receiver Jordyn Tyson and left tackle Kelvin Banks, cut running back Kendre Miller
articles.summary: NEW ORLEANS (AP) — New Orleans Saints receiver Jordyn Tyson, the club's 2026 first-round draft choice, is set to make his NFL debut as early as Sunday agains...
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS (AP) — New Orleans Saints receiver Jordyn Tyson, the club's 2026 first-round draft choice, is set to make his NFL debut as early as Sunday against the Cleveland Browns after being moved from injured reserve to the active roster.

The addition of Tyson to the active roster on Saturday was among a handful of moves by the Saints, who also activated second-year left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve, cut running back Kendre Miller and promoted kicker Charlie Smyth from the practice squad.

Tyson, drafted eighth overall out of Arizona State, injured his hamstring during training camp, and began the regular season on New Orleans' injured reserve list.

The 22-year-old receiver returned to practice on Wednesday on a limited basis, but said he felt physically ready to play.

The 6-foot-2, 203-pound Tyson — whose brother, Jaylon, plays in the NBA with Cleveland — was the second receiver drafted behind Ohio State's Carnell Tate, who went fourth overall to Tennessee.

Last season, Tyson played in nine games at Arizona State, catching 61 passes for 711 yards and eight touchdowns in a season shortened by a hamstring injuries in both legs.

Miller was in his fourth NFL season since the Saints made him a third-round draft choice out of TCU. Plagued by various injuries, he has yet to appear in more than eight games, or gain more than 193 yards rushing, in a season.

He has played in six games this season, gaining 159 yards and two touchdowns rushing on 57 carries to go with nine receptions for 37 yards.

Banks has not played since injuring his ankle during a Week 2 victory at Baltimore. Smyth, an international pathway player from Northern Ireland, has not played since the latter part of last season. He began this season on the practice squad after the Saints signed veteran kicker Daniel Carlson.

But Carlson was cut this past week on the heels of his fourth missed field goal this season.

The Saints also promoted running back Zamir White from the practice squad and cut tight end Treyton Welch.

articles.title: Patriots activate Mack Hollins from injured reserve on eve of Week 9
articles.summary: Sunday’s kickoff at Gillette Stadium is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.
articles.body:
Mack Hollins will get the green light against the Green Bay Packers.

The New England Patriots officially activated the veteran wide receiver on the eve of Sunday's game at Gillette Stadium.

A calf injury had sent Hollins to injured reserve a week into October. After missing the NFL minimum of four games, he saw his 21-day practice window open as the calendar turned to November. Three limited sessions and a questionable game designation followed.

Hollins, 33, now returns as the eldest statesman on an active depth chart of four. With A.J. Brown ruled out for a second consecutive matchup due to a knee injury and Romeo Doubs still residing on injured reserve due to a shoulder injury , DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III will make up the rest of the wideout room for the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

At the time of his non-contact exit last month at Highmark Stadium, Hollins stood atop the offense with 20 targets, 15 catches and 209 yards through four appearances. The 6-foot-4, 221-pound North Carolina product finds himself 131 games, 56 starts, 223 catches, 2,828 yards and 17 touchdowns into a career that began with the Philadelphia Eagles in the fourth round of the 2017 NFL draft at No. 118 overall.

A Super Bowl LII champion, Hollins made subsequent stops with the Miami Dolphins, Las Vegas Raiders, Atlanta Falcons and Buffalo Bills before arriving in Foxborough on a two-year deal in 2025.

New England carried an open spot on the 53-man roster after releasing and retaining veteran cornerback Kindle Vildor on the practice squad ahead of the Green Bay visit. No standard elevations were made for Sunday afternoon.

Tight end Hunter Henry, offensive tackle Morgan Moses, cornerback Carlton Davis III and safeties Kevin Byard III and Brenden Schooler move forward with questionable game statuses, while guard Greg Van Roten will remain on injured reserve after also having his practice window open at the start of the week.

articles.title: Broncos activate WR Pat Bryant from the IR and place DL Eyioma Uwazurike on the IR
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos announced today that they have activated wide receiver Pat Bryant from the injured reserve to the active roster and also placed defensive...
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos announced today that they have activated wide receiver Pat Bryant from the injured reserve to the active roster and also placed defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike on the injured reserve with a shoulder injury.

The team also announced it signed reserve cornerback Sam Fresch Jr. from the practice squad to the active roster.

Bryant returning to the offense will give the Broncos' passing offense a big boost moving forward. The second-year wide receiver was the star of training camp and was establishing himself as a key member of the offense prior to his injury. Now, he will join Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton as the Broncos' starting wide receivers moving forward.

As for Uwazurike, this is a bit of a loss for the Broncos' defense. He has been a key rotational piece who has played significant snaps thus far this season. With him sidelined, I wonder if we will see rookie defensive lineman Tyler Onyedim make his debut for the team tomorrow vs. the Panthers? He was the Broncos' first pick in April's 2026 NFL Draft, but has been a weekly inactive thus far this season. With Uwazurike now sidelined for at least four games, Onyedim may get a shot to prove himself. The team also has veteran Jordan Jackson on the roster, whom they could use as well. We could also see second-year defensive lineman Sai'vion Jones get some added snaps as well.

Former UFL player Sam Fresch Jr. has spent the season on the Broncos' practice squad and has been elevated a handful of times while Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss were sidelined. Now, with reserve cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine ruled out for Sunday's game, the team decided to add Fresch Jr. to the 53-man roster. He'll serve as the Broncos 5th corner while also giving the team another player with return ability in the kicking game.

So, the Broncos received some good news of the offensive side of the ball with the return of Pat Bryant, but also received some bad news with the loss of Uwazurike.

articles.body:
New York Jets general manager Darren Mougey appears to be ramping up his prep for the 2027 NFL draft.

The second-year general manager was seen speaking with Oklahoma State Cowboys offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Sean Brophy before the team's matchup against the Kansas State Wildcats on Saturday.

If Mougey was visiting Kansas to watch Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker, he likely left the game impressed. Mestemaker completed 22 of 28 pass attempts for 313 passing yards with four touchdowns and an interception in a 66-28 victory.

Mestemaker is projected to be the first quarterback selected in the 2027 NFL Draft, according to Mock Draft Database . The Jets currently hold three first-round picks in the upcoming draft, including two they acquired before last year's trade deadline by shipping cornerback Sauce Gardner to the Indianapolis Colts and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to the Dallas Cowboys.

If the NFL season ended today, all three of those picks would be among the top 10 selections, according to NFL's Chad Reuter . New York's highest selection would be their own, which is currently the No. 5 overall pick. That may not be high enough to select Mestemaker, especially since the Miami Dolphins — who currently hold the No. 2 pick — are likely looking for a franchise quarterback of their own.

articles.title: Vikings' Jauan Jennings Explains Why He Turned Down Trade to Return to 49ers
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings explained to reporters Saturday why he turned down the opportunity to return to his former team, the San Francisco 49ers, via trade.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings explained to reporters Saturday why he turned down the opportunity to return to his former team, the San Francisco 49ers, via trade.

"I just thought it was best for both teams," Jennings told ESPN's Kevin Seifert . "No distractions. I love where I'm at."

Jennings played his first five NFL seasons with the 49ers. He enjoyed much success in town, amassing career-highs in receptions (77) and receiving yards (975) in 2024 and touchdowns (nine) in 2025.

Last offseason, Jennings signed a one-year, $8 million contract with the Vikings, putting him in line to be WR3 in town alongside starters Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.

This season hasn't featured much production from Jennings (or much of the Vikings' pass game), though. Through six games, Jennings has just six catches and 54 yards (no touchdowns) on 10 targets.

Jennings had the opportunity to back to San Francisco, per a report from Fox Sports' Jay Glazer last Sunday, but he turned it down (49-second mark).

"The 49ers, who already traded for DeForest Buckner, also had a trade term worked out for Jauan Jennings," Glazer said. "It was contingent upon him hopping on a FaceTime call with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch and saying, 'Yeah, I want to come back,' but he didn't."

"He said, 'Actually, no, I want to stay here in Minnesota,'" Glazer said. "He likes what is going on in Minnesota."

San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan also had this to say.

"He likes where he's at," Shanahan said earlier this week, per Seifert, "and I thought he made sense [with] what he said, and I agreed with him."

Numerous San Francisco wideouts have suffered injuries this year. Mike Evans (ribs) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) are out this week. Ricky Pearsall will miss the entire season with a PCL injury, and De'Zhaun Stribling (left ankle deltoid ligament sprain) has been out since Week 1.

So the 6-1 49ers, who lead the NFC West, can certainly use Jennings. However, Jennings will stick in Minnesota with the 6-1 Vikings, who sit first in the NFC North.

Jennings and the Vikings will play next on Monday vs. the 6-1 Buffalo Bills.

articles.title: Bill Belichick Reacts to Rob Gronkowski's Patriots HOF Induction, TE Among 'Best of All Time'
articles.summary: UNC football head coach Bill Belichick offered great praise for former New England Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski, who he coached on the Pats from 2010-2018.
articles.body:
UNC football head coach Bill Belichick offered great praise for former New England Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski, who he coached on the Pats from 2010-2018.

The Patriots inducted Gronkowski into the team's Hall of Fame on Saturday, the same day that Belichick led his Tar Heels to a 38-21 road win over UConn.

Gronkowski had this to say about Belichick during his Friday press conference, per Mark Daniels and Karen Guregian of MassLive.

"He played a tremendous role in who I am as a player. I really loved the way he challenged me," Gronkowski said. "He's the best football coach I've ever seen in my life, that I've ever been a part of as well. … I thank him for that and I wouldn't be here without him."

When Belichick was told of Gronkowski's remarks, he offered these comments, per Matt Vautour of Mass Live.

"That's nice of Rob to say that. I talked to Rob and congratulated him on his selection into the Patriots Hall of Fame. Well deserved. He was the best tight end in football during his time and one of the best of all time. I'm proud of Rob and what he's accomplished.

"He came a long, long way from barely playing in college at Arizona, to where he ended up, which was an incredible credit to him, his work ethic, his toughness and his dependability. It's a hard position to play, but he excelled at it. We wouldn't have won as many games as we did without him, I can tell you that. He's a big part of it. I love Rob."

Gronkowski played nine of his 11 seasons with the Pats, winning three Super Bowls and making four All-Pro First Teams and five Pro Bowls. In 115 regular season games with New England, Gronkowski caught 521 passes for 7,861 yards and 79 touchdowns. Belichick was around for all of it as part of his 24 seasons as the Patriots' head coach.

Now New England will honor Gronkowski at halftime of the Patriots' home game against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Steelers' Mason McCormick Not Fined After Being Called Out by Browns' Jared Verse for Body Slam
articles.summary: The NFL will not fine Pittsburgh Steelers offensive guard Mason McCormick for slamming Cleveland Browns defensive end Jared Verse to the turf in Week 8.
articles.body:
The NFL will not fine Pittsburgh Steelers offensive guard Mason McCormick for slamming Cleveland Browns defensive end Jared Verse to the turf in Week 8.

McCormick grabbed Verse mid-air and forcefully threw him to the ground following an extra-point attempt during the Steelers' 27-6 victory. The play resulted in a 15-yard penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct.

Verse voiced his displeasure with McCormick — and with his teammates for not defending him — after the game, but it evidently wasn't enough to sway the league.

Verse made strong comments about the Steelers ahead of the game. The 26-year-old said he wasn't "worried about their [offensive] line" and that the Browns planned on making "Pittsburgh ours."

The NFL levied 31 fines in Week 8 , the second-highest total for any week this season. Among those was McCormick's teammate, Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker, who was hit with a $17,911 fine for a hit to the head on Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. Three Browns players — Tyson Campbell, Quinshon Judkins and Sam Williams — each received fines for either unsportsmanlike conduct or unnecessary roughness.

The Browns entered the game atop the AFC North due to tiebreakers, but the loss dropped them to third in the division. The Steelers moved into first with a 6-2 record after avenging their 27-24 loss against Cleveland in Week 4.

articles.body:
Sunday night at Soldier Field closes out a three-game prime-time stretch for a 6-2 Bears team that just beat the defending Super Bowl champions in Seattle. Several prominent national analysts have pointed to this game as a trap/upset in the making. What follows are our score pick, winner, and projected stat lines for a Sunday Night Football matchup that could push Chicago deeper into the NFC race.

Sunday, November 8, 2026 , at Soldier Field .

Radio: ESPN Chicago (1000 AM / 100.3 FM HD2) and LATINO MIX 93.5 FM (Spanish)

National broadcast team is Mike Tirico (play-by-play), Cris Collinsworth (analyst), and Melissa Stark (sideline). Local Bears radio is Jeff Joniak, Tom Thayer, and Jason McKie.

Josh : I think the Bucs get their yards in the air this game, with Chicago's depleted secondary giving up a pair of scores and the run game getting them into field goal range. By contrast, I think Chicago's offense doesn't miss a beat and they hang a pair through the air and a pair on the ground with a Santos field goal to round it out. 31-17 Bears.

Jeff Berckes : There's something about what this Bears team is building, where we're at on the schedule, and the narrative that feels like there's an outburst coming. Bears 41 – Bucs 13.

Sam : I'm no longer scared of good defenses. But that doesn't make this game a walk in the park. The Bears are due for a letdown.
