articles.title: Broncos and Bo Nix have won 16 straight one-score games
articles.summary: The Broncos keep finding ways to win games — especially close games.
articles.body:
The Broncos keep finding ways to win games — especially close games.

Denver has won 16 straight games decided by one score or less. Quarterback Bo Nix has been the starter in each of the games.

Via NBC Sports research, the streak ties the 2023-24 Chiefs (with starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes) for the longest streak since 1950.

The Broncos last lost a one-score game in Week 3 of the 2025 season, 23-20 at the Chargers. Since then, the Broncos have won every one-score game in which they have played.

This year, they're doing it despite being routinely outgained. For the season, they have a yardage differential of minus-658 — third worst in the NFL. And the Broncos have won three games in 2026 despite being outgained by 100 or more yards.

The record for any season is four wins, accomplished by eight different teams. With two more this year, the Broncos will have the record to themselves.

The next opportunity to win a one-score game comes on Sunday, at the Panthers in a rematch of Super Bowl 50.

articles.title: “Don’t even come close”: Travis Kelce under fire as New England Patriots legend Rob Ninkovich makes bold Rob Gronkowski comparison during Hall of Fame ceremony

Burrow is a noted Pokémon fan, wearing a Pikachu-themed neck pillow as the Bengals traveled to Spain to face the Falcons.

The three-time Pro Bowler has started his 2026 campaign on a high note, completing 73.0 percent of his passes for 2,115 yards and a league-leading 20 touchdowns in seven games. He's also been picked off just six times.

Burrow has helped the Bengals begin the year with a 5-2 record, holding to No. 2 spot in the AFC North standings.

Kickoff between Atlanta and Cincinnati on Sunday is at 9:30 a.m. ET.

articles.summary: Atlanta Falcons y Cincinnati Bengals se miden en un duelo apasionante, en el que será el segundo partido de la historia de la NFL en España
articles.body: Las siete estrellas que dibujan la bandera de Madrid bajarán del cielo este domingo para posarse sobre el césped del Santiago Bernabéu. Kyle Pitts, Bijan Robinson, Drake London, Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins y Joe Burrow forman una constelación difícil de reunir en cualquier rincón del planeta. La séptima estrella no lleva casco ni hombreras, es el propio Bernabéu, el Coliseo Blanco, que abre de nuevo sus puertas a la NFL en el segundo partido de su historia y lo hace con un cartel que promete deslumbrar. El estadio ya está listo. El césped, las yardas pintadas y los postes amarillos han transformado el templo del madridismo en un escenario de fútbol americano, y quienes lo han pisado estos días no han escondido su asombro. Jugadores y técnicos de ambos equipos han recorrido el Coliseo Blanco con la mirada de quien entra por primera vez en una catedral. Saben que hoy, a las 15:30, no jugarán un partido más. Porque en juego hay mucho más que un espectáculo. Atlanta y Cincinnati llegan con sus conferencias en el horizonte, y una victoria en Madrid puede valer media temporada. Todo apunta a un festival ofensivo: dos ataques con talento de sobra, armas en cada posición y la promesa de un marcador alto. Los Bengals aterrizan en España convertidos en un vendaval. Con un balance de 5-2, segundos en la AFC Norte, han superado los 30 puntos en cada uno de sus últimos tres partidos. El último, una locura de 43-36 en la prórroga ante Tennessee, en la que Burrow firmó 462 yardas y cinco touchdowns. El quarterback vive la mejor racha de su carrera y tiene a su lado a la pareja de receptores más temida de la liga. Chase es electricidad pura con el balón en las manos, y Higgins, elegido Jugador Ofensivo de la Semana en la AFC, es el complemento perfecto. Es un ataque que vive en el aire y castiga cualquier descuido de la secundaria rival. Los Falcons, que ejercen como locales, llegan con más dudas que certezas. Su 3-5 y la dolorosa derrota por 16-0 ante Tampa Bay, en condiciones casi de huracán, les obligan a reaccionar. Michael Penix Jr. lanzó cuatro intercepciones aquel día y busca en Madrid su redención. Su juego se basa en soltar el balón rápido, y para ello tiene a London, que suma 624 yardas, y a Pitts, máximo anotador del equipo con cuatro touchdowns. Pero el corazón de Atlanta late en las piernas de Bijan Robinson, líder de la NFL en yardas de carrera con 780 y un promedio de 5,2 por acarreo. Enfrente tendrá a una defensa que es de las que mejor frena el juego terrestre. Este domingo, Madrid mirará al cielo y lo encontrará sobre la hierba. Siete estrellas, un estadio legendario y un partido que aspira a quedarse para siempre en la memoria del Coliseo Blanco. Cambiarán el balón, las reglas y los héroes, pero no la magia y la mística de un templo que nació para ver brillar a los mejores.

articles.summary: La NFL vuelve al Bernabéu
articles.body: Madrid vuelve a ser la capital del fútbol americano este domingo. El 8 de noviembre a las 15:30 h, el 2026 NFL Madrid Game enfrentará a Cincinnati Bengals y Atlanta Falcons en el Santiago Bernabéu. Es el duelo de la semana 9 de la temporada regular, con los Falcons como local designado. En España habrá varias formas de seguirlo. DAZN lo emitirá en abierto y sin suscripción, y Cuatro lo retransmitirá en abierto. También estará en Mediaset Infinity y en NFL Game Pass dentro de DAZN. La prueba gratuita de siete días de Game Pass termina el 9 de noviembre. Será el segundo partido oficial de la NFL en territorio español. En el estreno, los Dolphins ganaron 16-13 en la prórroga a los Commanders. Esta vez se esperan unos 80.000 aficionados, frente a los 78.610 de 2025, y todavía quedan entradas. El descanso tendrá música. El colombiano Manuel Turizo encabezará el espectáculo del intermedio, que deberá ajustarse a la normativa local de ruido. Los organizadores también preparan un homenaje sorpresa a las víctimas del accidente ferroviario de la semana pasada.

articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK - Monday night when the Buffalo Bills take on the Minnesota Vikings , Josh Allen will be back at the place where his legend first began taking shape.

Buffalo's only previous visit to U.S. Bank Stadium came in Week 3 of the 2018 season, and for Allen it was just his second NFL start. The odds were stacked against him and the Bills, literally, as the wise guys in Las Vegas installed the Bills as 17-point underdogs.

But the newbie quarterback stunned NFL nation and during the Bills' 27-6 blowout victory , he authored the first of probably about 100 meme-worthy plays, his never-to-be-forgotten leap over Vikings linebacker Anthony Barr . From that moment on he's been a nonstop highlight reel.

As is typically his way, he didn't have much to say about the play because, as we've learned, Allen is very much a live-in-the-moment kind of guy, not one to dwell on past performances.

"Honestly, not really," he said when he was asked if it had crossed his mind that he's returning to the scene of that first big play.

But he did eventually elaborate when he was asked again about whether he was surprised by the crazy reaction that play got on social media with all the memes and later the t-shirts that were emblazoned with the picture of him leaping over Barr.

"Surprised me, too," he said. "I was a good athlete in college. High school I was not. So as I got older and started to lift more weights, I guess I got a little more athletic. But yeah, I think it was just kind of a surprising thing for me too of what I was able to do, especially early on in the career with the running stuff. I know I still run a little bit now, but that was I think the moment that I was like, 'You know what? I do belong here.'"

He then immediately spun forward and talked about how playing there will be nice in that there won't be any weather to worry about, though it will be a difficult environment because of the Vikings' passionate supporters who make that dome among the loudest venues in the NFL.

"They're going to be a loud fan base," he said. "Them being what their record is and kind of rolling right now, and their defense is playing outstanding football, so we're expecting an extremely loud crowd. That's a really, really good crowd. That's what I do remember about being there, early in that game just how loud it was, and they've got their Skol chant, which is an awesome tradition. It's going to be a fun experience."
